title: Starter Bridge: SDK Interop & Handoff Checklist (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a tiny, high-leverage "starter bridge" that helps product engineers and solutions teams hand off a minimal, production-ready SDK integration to customers. The focus is interop (multiple languages / runtime shapes), predictable telemetry, and a one-page quickstart that actually works end-to-end for a sample use-case (chat + streaming + basic error recovery).

Audience:
- SDK engineers and tech writers (primary)
- Solutions engineers and onboarding PMs (secondary)
- Early pilot customers (read-only)

Why:
- We keep seeing handoffs fail because the onramp doc assumes lots of infra knowledge. We need a distilled checklist + tiny repo that covers the 80% paths that break in the first week.
- Goal is < 90 minutes from "account created" to a running demo that calls the hosted API, streams, and gracefully falls back on a local stub.

Success metrics (how we will know this helped):
- First-call success rate for pilot customers increases from ~56% to >80% within two weeks of using the bridge.
- Time-to-demo (median) measured from signup->demo < 90m in observability tests.
- Fewer support tickets about "can't stream" or "timeouts" in first 72h.

High-level flow (one-page quickstart sketch):
1) Create API key + set env var (REDWOOD_KEY)
2) Clone tiny repo (starter-bridge) and run `make demo`
3) Open http://localhost:3000 -> type prompt -> watch streaming tokens and fallback behavior
4) Inspect telemetry: trace ID printed in console -> paste into Console trace search
5) Optional: swap to local stub (instructions) to validate local dev loop

Tiny repo contents (minimum):
- README-onepage.md (the one-page quickstart)
- samples/chat-streaming/{js,py} (two tiny clients)
- local-stub/ (very small HTTP stub to mimic streaming semantics)
- e2e-check.sh (smoke test: sign-in -> call -> stream -> assert)

Interop checklist (must-pass):
- [ ] Auth header sample present in each language (curl, node, python)
- [ ] Streaming example that shows incremental token output (not just chunked body)
- [ ] Error contract example: how to detect 429, 503, and how to fallback to stub
- [ ] Telemetry: include trace_id in every client log line and surface instructions to map to Console
- [ ] Retry/backoff snippet: idempotency keys for non-chat endpoints documented
- [ ] Minimal dependency installs: keep runtime overhead < 3 packages for sample app

SDK surface sanity tests (dev checklist):
- run `samples/js/demo.js` and confirm streaming latency < 500ms for first chunk in test env
- run `samples/py/demo.py` and confirm it prints trace id and final token count
- run local-stub and force 503 to verify client fallback paths

Telemetry & observability minimal contract (to include in README):
- Required: log lines must include `trace_id=<hex>` and `request_id=<uuid>`
- Optional but recommended: include `model`, `prompt_hash`, and `tokens_generated`
- Mapping: console -> search by trace_id; every sample must show a link template to open the Console trace (paste trace id into URL)

Handoff checklist for solutions engineers (practical):
- [ ] Create tenant and generate onboarding key with restricted scope for demo
- [ ] Pair-run the demo with customer (share screen) and capture the first failing step
- [ ] If streaming fails: capture client logs, copy trace_id, escalate to eng-developer-experience with GH/PR reference
- [ ] Confirm that the customer can run local-stub and reproduce offline flow
- [ ] Add notes to customer onboarding ticket (JIRA) with exact commands run

Common gotchas and quick fixes (notes):
- Missing newline flush in Node streaming example -> add `res.flushHeaders()` and `res.write()` cadence note
- Proxy / corp firewall causes truncated streaming: call out `Connection: keep-alive` and suggest stubbing with `curl --no-buffer`
- Long prompts exceed default token budget: include a debug snippet to print `model_context_window` and the server-side truncation warning in logs

Rollout plan (pilot -> GA):
- Week 0: internal dry run with SEs (this doc + tiny repo)
- Week 1: 3 pilot customers (SE-led pairing sessions) and rapid fixes from feedback
- Week 2: expand to 15 customers, instrument first-call metric in Console dashboards
- Week 4: ship as "Starter Bridge" template in Console + add "Create demo tenant" button in onboarding flow

Open questions (TODOs / unresolved):
- Which default model should samples use? (ola-3-small vs widely used community model) -> action: @Ravi to propose by 2025-02-25
- Do we include embedded examples in the same repo or link to embedder quickstart? (tradeoff: repo size vs discoverability)
- What telemetry retention level do we require for starter tenants? Need legal/infra input.

Immediate next steps (ownerable):
- Ava: scaffold tiny repo and README-onepage.md, include both js/py streaming examples (ETA 2025-02-18)
- Ravi: pick default model and add model param to samples (ETA 2025-02-25)
- Eleni: draft Console trace link template and minimal dashboard for first-call metric (ETA 2025-02-20)
- Marcus: write e2e-check.sh that can run in CI and assert streaming and fallback behavior (ETA 2025-02-21)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep the one-page quickstart intentionally opinionated: one path that works. Add "variations" sections for advanced users but hide by default.
- Consider making local-stub an executable container so SEs don't need Docker experience but can still run it quickly.
- We should add a "diagnostics" endpoint that prints effective request limits and last 5 trace IDs to make pairing sessions easier.

History / context:
- Pulled from recurring SE feedback (Jan 2025 onboarding retro) and several GH issues where samples were missing trace ids. This doc is meant as the leanest thing that meaningfully raises first-call success for new customers.

End.
